title: Safety First Approach

nodes.text: Adopt the Safe Person Approach (SPA) and use the Dynamic Risk Assessment (DRA) process to minimize risk

evidence.source_text: By adopting the SPA and using the DRA process you can minimise the risk of injury to self and others.

nodes.text: Deploy lookouts (fixed, aerial, or mobile) to maintain risk awareness and provide timely advice on escape routes and safety zones

evidence.source_text: Lookouts | A fixed, aerial or mobile lookout shall be deployed to maintain a clear appreciation of risks and to provide timely advice of the need to use of escape routes and safety zones.

nodes.text: Ensure firefighters are aware of changes in fire behaviour due to fuel, weather, topography, and other hazards

evidence.source_text: Awareness | Firefighters shall be aware of the impact of changes in fire behaviour including those resulting from variations to fuel, weather and topography and of other fireground hazards.

nodes.text: Follow the Communications Plan and communicate with crew and surrounding crews to address safety issues

evidence.source_text: Communications | All fire crews shall follow the Communications Plan, communicate with your crew and surrounding crews to discuss and address safety issues.

nodes.text: Agree on at least two escape routes and ensure they are known to all personnel; continually review their suitability

evidence.source_text: Escape Routes | At least two escape routes should be agreed and made known to all relevant personnel. The suitability of an escape route should be continually reviewed to ensure it remains effective.

nodes.text: Identify safety zones and ensure they are known to all firefighters; consider escape time and zone size as fire behaviour changes

evidence.source_text: Safety Zones | Safety zones should be identified and made known to all relevant firefighters. Firefighters need to consider escape time and safety zone size requirements that will change as fire behaviour changes.

nodes.text: Report OHS incidents via the chain of command and agency's reporting system

evidence.source_text: This does not replace the need to immediately communicate these incidents via the chain of command. Personnel will be required to report OHS incidents via their own agency’s reporting system.
